title: Extension by zero of a Frobenius coefficient morphism
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum and the coefficient ring
$A=A_{E,n}$. Let $j_0:X_0\hookrightarrow\bar X_0$ be a
compactification over $k_0$ of a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme,
with base change $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ to $k$, and write
$\Phi=\Phi_X$, $\bar\Phi=\Phi_{\bar X}$ for the $q$-power scheme
Frobenii of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. For $m\geq0$ let

$$
b_m:L\bar\Phi^{m*}j_!\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j_!L\Phi^{m*}
$$

be the comparison isomorphism of [lem-trf-open-square-exchange] for the
Cartesian square of [lem-trf-frobenius-open-square] with
$(h,\bar h)=(\Phi^m,\bar\Phi^m)$. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ carry an
explicit etale-origin witness [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness].

1. *Extension of coefficient morphisms.* For every morphism
$v:L\Phi^{m*}K\to K$ put
$$
\bar v=j_!v\circ b_m:\;L\bar\Phi^{m*}j_!K\longrightarrow j_!K .
$$
If $\psi:L\Phi^*K\to K$ is a Frobenius coefficient morphism of
[def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism] (no invertibility assumed),
then $\bar\psi$ is a Frobenius coefficient morphism on
$j_!K\in D^b_{ctf}(\bar X,A)$, and its iterates are the extensions of
the iterates of $\psi$:
$$
(\bar\psi)_m=\overline{\psi_m}=j_!\psi_m\circ b_m\qquad(m\geq1).
$$
1. *Stalks.* Let $\bar y$ be a geometric point of $\bar X$ with
$\bar\Phi^m\bar y=\bar y$, and let $\bar v_{\bar y}$ be the endomorphism of the pro-etale geometric stalk [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk] $(j_!K)_{\bar y}$ induced by $\bar v$ through
$(L\bar\Phi^{m*}j_!K)_{\bar y}\cong(j_!K)_{\bar y}$. If $\bar y$ lies in
$X$, let $v_{\bar y}$ be the endomorphism of $K_{\bar y}$ induced by $v$ through
$(L\Phi^{m*}K)_{\bar y}\cong K_{\bar y}$; then $(j_!K)_{\bar y}=K_{\bar y}$ and $\bar v_{\bar y}=v_{\bar y}$;
otherwise $(j_!K)_{\bar y}=0$.
1. *Global operators.* For the graph correspondences
$c=(\operatorname{id}_X,\Phi^m)$ and
$\bar c=(\operatorname{id}_{\bar X},\bar\Phi^m)$ of
[def-trf-graph-correspondence], the comparison
$C_{j,K}:R\Gamma_c(X,K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(\bar X,j_!K)$ of
[lem-trf-compactification-cohomology] intertwines the global
operators of [def-trf-global-operator]:
$$
C_{j,K}\circ T_c(v)=T_{\bar c}(\bar v)\circ C_{j,K}.
$$

proof.text:
*(1).* The complex $j_!K$ lies in $D^b_{ctf}(\bar X,A)$ by
[lem-trf-open-ctf], so $\bar\psi$ is a Frobenius coefficient morphism
on it. For the iterates, argue by induction on $m$, the case $m=1$
being the definition. The squares of [lem-trf-frobenius-open-square]
for $\bar\Phi$ and $\bar\Phi^{m-1}$ paste to the square for
$\bar\Phi^m$, so by the pasting clause of
[lem-trf-open-square-exchange], after the pullback composition
identifications,
$b_m=b_{1,L\Phi^{(m-1)*}K}\circ L\bar\Phi^*b_{m-1}$. Using the
recursion of [def-trf-frobenius-coefficient-morphism], the induction
hypothesis, and the naturality of $b_1$,

$$
(\bar\psi)_m=\bar\psi\circ L\bar\Phi^*(\bar\psi)_{m-1}
=j_!\psi\circ b_1\circ L\bar\Phi^*j_!\psi_{m-1}\circ
L\bar\Phi^*b_{m-1}
=j_!\psi\circ j_!L\Phi^*\psi_{m-1}\circ b_{1}\circ L\bar\Phi^*b_{m-1}
=j_!\psi_m\circ b_m .
$$

*(2).* Apply [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero] to the finite ring $A$ and the open immersion $j$. It acts degreewise and gives $(j_!K)_{\bar y}=K_{\bar y}$ inside $X$ and zero outside. By [lem-exc-proetale-open-unit], restriction identifies $j^*j_!$ with the identity; this identification holds termwise on complexes, since the two functors are exact by [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. The normalization in [lem-trf-open-square-exchange] identifies $j^*b_m$ with the identity. Thus restriction of $j_!v\circ b_m$ is $v$. Applying the geometric stalk functor at the fixed geometric point inside $X$ gives the same endomorphism, with the same pullback-to-stalk identification. No stalk-detection claim for arbitrary pro-etale complexes is used.

*(3a): witnessed domains.* Write $M=L\Phi^{m*}K$. Apply [lem-trf-witnessed-open-pullback] with $u=\Phi^m$, $i=j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ and the given witness $(L,\alpha)$. It supplies $L_m=(\Phi^m_{\mathrm{et}})^{-1}L$, the witness $\alpha_m$ for $M$, and the specified witnesses $(j^{\mathrm{et}}_!L,j_!\alpha\circ\delta_{j,L})$ for $j_!K$ and $(j^{\mathrm{et}}_!L_m,j_!\alpha_m\circ\delta_{j,L_m})$ for $j_!M$. Pullback preserves the stated constructible finite-Tor domain by [thm-sf-ctf-stability], clause (i). Thus $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and [lem-trf-compactification-cohomology] defines $C_{j,M}$ on its displayed witness; all subsequent compact-support comparisons are on their witnessed domains.

*(3b): proper iterates.* Put $h=\Phi^m$ and $\bar h=\bar\Phi^m$. They are $k$-morphisms by [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. For $m=0$ they are identities, hence finite. The base Frobenii are finite by [lem-trf-scheme-frobenius-finite-radicial], and induction using [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition] makes every positive iterate finite. Hence both maps are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. The Cartesian square is the square of [lem-trf-frobenius-open-square].

*(3c): the operator formulas and comparison.* By [prop-trf-graph-operator],
$$T_c(v)=R\Gamma_c(X,v)\circ\iota_X\circ R\Gamma_c(X,\eta),\qquad
T_{\bar c}(\bar v)=R\Gamma(\bar X,\bar v)\circ\iota_{\bar X}\circ R\Gamma(\bar X,\bar\eta),$$
where $\eta:K\to Rh_*M$ and $\bar\eta:j_!K\to R\bar h_*L\bar h^*j_!K$ are the ordinary units. Here $\iota_X$ and $\iota_{\bar X}$ use proper coincidence and compact-support composition for $a_Xh=a_X$ and $a_{\bar X}\bar h=a_{\bar X}$; the proper target identifies its ordinary and compact cohomology by [prop-functor-package]. Define
$$\gamma:j_!Rh_*M\xrightarrow{\sim}R\bar h_*j_!M$$
by composing the compact-support comparisons for $jh=\bar h j$, with proper coincidence for $h,\bar h$ ([prop-functor-package], clause (3)). Use the canonical choice-independent composition and identity normalization of [thm-sf-comp-composition] throughout.

source.place: *(3)*, graph formulas and definition of gamma

proof.text:
*Step A: the units.* Apply [lem-trf-finite-horizontal-shriek-mate] to $f=f'=j$, $p=h=\Phi^m$, $g=\bar h=\bar\Phi^m$: the square is Cartesian by [lem-trf-frobenius-open-square], $g$ is finite by (3b), and $K\in D^b_{ctf}$. For its $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ use the compactification $(j,\operatorname{id}_{\bar X})$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], whose base change along $\bar h$ is again $(j,\operatorname{id}_{\bar X})$. In [def-exchange-projection], $\operatorname{Ex}_{*,\mathrm{id}}$ is built from the identity adjunction and pullback composition, hence is the identity by [fix-prop-coherence]; so $\operatorname{Ex}_{!,K}=\beta_K$, the open base change of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change]. By [lem-cbc-finite-open-exchange-scalars] with $a=\operatorname{id}_A$, $\beta_K^{-1}$ is the $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ adjunct of $h^{-1}u_K$ followed by the composition comparison for $\bar hj=jh$, with $u_K$ the unit, invertible by [lem-exc-proetale-open-unit]; so $\beta_K$ restricts to the identity on $X$ after the pullback identifications. So does $b_{m,K}$, by [lem-trf-open-square-exchange]. A map out of $j_!M$ is determined by its adjunct under the exact degreewise adjunction of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]; hence $\beta_K=b_{m,K}=\operatorname{Ex}_{!,K}$. The theorem's $\chi_M$ is $\gamma_M$: both use the same compact-support composition/proper-coincidence maps for $jh=\bar hj$. Its unit equation gives
$$\gamma\circ j_!\eta=R\bar h_*b_m\circ\bar\eta:j_!K\longrightarrow R\bar h_*j_!M.$$
This is the unit compatibility used in Step B.

source.place: *Step A: the units.*, normalized open-square mate specialization

proof.text:
*Step B: transport to cohomology.* The comparisons $C_{j,-}$ are
natural in the witnessed complex ([lem-trf-compactification-cohomology]),
so $C_{j,K}\circ R\Gamma_c(X,v)=R\Gamma(\bar X,j_!v)\circ C_{j,M}$.
They are compatible with the composition law of the compact-support
direct image ([thm-sf-comp-composition]: its canonical composition comparison is independent of all compactification choices; [fix-prop-coherence] gives the identity and composition coherence), which gives
$$
C_{j,M}\circ\iota_X\circ R\Gamma_c(X,\eta)
=\iota_{\bar X}\circ R\Gamma(\bar X,\gamma\circ j_!\eta)\circ C_{j,K}.
$$
Substituting Step A and $j_!v\circ b_m=\bar v$ (naturality of
$\iota_{\bar X}$ moves $R\bar\Phi^m_*b_m$ past it), one obtains
$C_{j,K}\circ T_c(v)=R\Gamma(\bar X,\bar v)\circ\iota_{\bar X}\circ
R\Gamma(\bar X,\bar\eta)\circ C_{j,K}=T_{\bar c}(\bar v)\circ C_{j,K}$.
No invertibility of $v$ is used anywhere.

proof_origin.place: Retained blueprint steps (1), (2), (3) and Steps A/B; witness-transport subargument extracted, properness and graph formulas separated, and the unit calculation supplied by the existing finite-horizontal mate theorem specialized to the open square.

Replaced old step 3 by witnessed-domain, properness and graph-formula steps, extracting the derived witness comparison into one unsplit node. Replaced old step 4 by the existing finite-horizontal shriek-mate statement specialized to the same open Frobenius square. Also cited the actual Frobenius finiteness theorem now named by its definition. Restored root citations.json and preserved all prior Mathlib search records.
split_report.blueprint: Original *(1)* and *(2)* are steps 1–2; *(3)* is steps 3–5, using lem-trf-witnessed-open-pullback for its derived witness subargument; Step A is step 6, using lem-trf-finite-horizontal-shriek-mate on the same open square; Step B is unchanged as step 7.

tool_uses.why: The finite-coefficient pro-etale exact open adjunction and geometric stalk formula are generic tools; the trace-formula unit has no such site theorem.
The generic pro-etale open unit is used to restrict maps out of j_!K; no trace-formula-unit node states this.
The established identity and composition coherence normalizes the proper/open comparison and the cohomology reassociation.
Canonical compact-support composition, on bounded-below etale-origin complexes and independent of choices, supplies precisely the compatibility absent from the refinement-only statement.
Generic scheme-morphism fact establishes properness of iterated Frobenius, as required by the graph-operator formula; the trace-formula unit has no separate finite-composition theorem.
Generic finite-implies-proper fact verifies the graph-operator hypothesis for positive Frobenius iterates; used as a scheme-theoretic tool only.

Its explicit finite-coefficient pullback clause (i) verifies the Dctf domain of the pulled-back complex; this is the generic preservation theorem of the six-functor package, not a replacement trace-formula route.
